content:
Apple has launched new Mac mini and Mac Studio models today, and alongside those releases, the company's lineup of Magic Keyboard accessories has also received some updates.

The latest Magic Keyboard removes the text labels from keys in favor of icons

Apple's Mac mini and Mac Studio get a big performance boost thanks to new chips including the next-generation M6 and the higher-end M5 Ultra.

You can pre-order the new models now: Mac mini here, Mac Studio here.

In addition to the desktop improvements, Apple has also updated its Magic Keyboard lineup, with a small change on the new models.

The latest Magic Keyboard removes the text labels from many keys, replacing them with symbols instead.

Apple made the same change earlier this year on the MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, and MacBook Pro. Now the Magic Keyboard is getting the same update.

The change applies to all of the new Magic Keyboard models:

  • Magic Keyboard: $99
  • Magic Keyboard with Touch ID: $149
  • Magic Keyboard with Touch ID and Numeric Keypad: $179

Common keys like tab, caps lock, return, shift, and delete drop their text labels in favor of just icons. On the extended model with the numeric keypad, Home, Page Up, and Page Down also feature new icons to replace the existing text.

Popular comment from Doug

Setting aside these symbol changes, can the pricing be more affordable?

$69, $99, and $129

I love Apple's keyboards, but $179 for the extended version with Touch ID is too expensive!

Apart from the switch to symbols, the new Magic Keyboard looks identical to the previous generation. They all feature USB-C, and the functionality and layout remain the same as before.

If you want to order the new Magic Keyboards from Amazon rather than Apple, you can grab them here: Magic Keyboard, with Touch ID, and with Touch ID and Numeric Keypad (in black).

What do you think about the keys dropping their text labels? Share your thoughts in the comments below.
